extracted.intended_audience: general readers and mathematicians interested in the history and practice of mathematical writing
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices used by the Nicolas Bourbaki collective for producing mathematical texts and seminars: the group's stylistic expectations (rigor, terseness, self-contained exposition), editorial process (reading drafts aloud, consensus), anonymity/collective authorship, and related publication norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous, formal, 'stripped to the logical studs' writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: “The most distinctive feature of Bourbaki was the writing style: rigorous, formal and stripped to the logical studs. The books spelled out mathematical theorems from the ground up without skipping any steps — exhibiting an unusual degree of thoroughness among mathematicians.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect complete, precise proofs with no gaps; write in a highly formal register. Anti-patterns: informal motivation, skipped steps, hand-wavy arguments. Trade-off: such precision can make texts hard to read because they do not offer contextualizing narrative or 'why' commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No contextualizing narrative — state and prove without commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: “They don’t offer a contextualizing narrative that explains where concepts come from, instead letting the ideas speak for themselves. 'You state stuff and prove it, and that’s it.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor terse exposition that focuses on definitions, statements, and proofs rather than historical/motivational explanation or examples. Anti-patterns: long pedagogical introductions, anecdotal motivation, or explanatory asides. If following this standard, omit commentary about intent or intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained, free-standing exposition (minimal outside references)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Free-standing books that explained advanced mathematics without reference to any outside sources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write texts so a reader can follow development without needing external textbooks or papers; include necessary prerequisites and definitions within the work. Anti-patterns: relying on external references to fill foundational gaps; assuming informal background knowledge without definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus-driven collaborative editing process
rubrics_metrics.description: “Once a member produces a draft, the group gathers in person, reads it aloud and suggests notes for revision. They repeat these steps until there is unanimous agreement that the text is ready for publication.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafts are subject to extensive group review: read-aloud sessions, iterative revision cycles, and acceptance only by unanimous approval. Practical implications: expect long review timelines and multiple rounds of precise edits. Anti-patterns: single-author unilateral publication, cursory peer review, or ignoring group feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of read-aloud collective review as an editorial tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Members 'read everything aloud year after year' as part of preparing and revising manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include oral reading and group discussion as a formal part of the editorial workflow to catch logical/linguistic issues and to achieve collective understanding. Anti-patterns: purely asynchronous or written-only review without in-person discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication only upon unanimous agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Texts are published only when every member agrees it is ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a publication condition that requires full group consensus (not majority). This increases thoroughness but lengthens timelines. Anti-patterns: majority-rule or editor-only final decisions when emulating Bourbaki practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term, slow-to-publish work intended to 'stand forever'
rubrics_metrics.description: The group’s process 'can take a decade or more to complete' and the work is meant to be long-lived rather than rapidly disseminated in draft form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize enduring completeness and permanence over fast preprint-style release; expect projects with multi-year or multi-decade timelines. Anti-patterns: rapid posting of drafts, prioritizing speed over completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on collective authorship and anonymity to highlight the mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Bourbaki remains a secret society to emphasize the collective nature of the work and to present the books as 'a pure expression of mathematics as it is, not an individual’s take on the topic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present work under a collective byline or otherwise de-emphasize individual credit to foreground the material. Note: anonymity is 'not rigidly enforced' in modern practice and may be more a cultural ethic than a strict rule. Anti-patterns: heavy individual self-promotion in contexts intended to be collective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventing and standardizing precise vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the first Bourbaki books 'invented vocabulary that is now standard — terms like "injective," "surjective" and "bijective."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When beneficial, coin clear, systematic terminology to disambiguate concepts and standardize usage across the field. Anti-patterns: ad-hoc or inconsistent terminology that impedes clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment moderation standards for the article's discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Quanta Magazine moderates comments to facilitate an informed, substantive, civil conversation. Abusive, profane, self-promotional, misleading, incoherent or off-topic comments will be rejected. Moderators are staffed during regular business hours (New York time) and can only accept comments written in English."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For participation in the article's comment thread: keep posts civil, on-topic, substantive, non-promotional, coherent, truthful, and in English; expect moderation during NY business hours. Anti-patterns: abusive language, promotion, off-topic threads, incoherent posts, non-English submissions.
